test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Under which Indian Act has the Central Bureau of Investigation been empowered to apprehend and prosecute wildlife offenders?

options.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 was enacted by the Government of India to protect the country's wild animals, birds, and plant species in order to ensure environmental and ecological security.
 
• This act provides a legal framework for the protection of various species of flora and fauna, and also for the establishment of protected areas such as sanctuaries and national parks.
 
• The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has been empowered under this act to apprehend and prosecute wildlife offenders, ensuring stringent enforcement of the law.
 
• The act also stipulates the punishment for offenses committed against wildlife, which includes both fines and imprisonment, thereby acting as a deterrent against wildlife crimes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**

 
 
• This act aims to prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering on animals and to amend the law relating to the prevention of cruelty to animals.
 
• It led to the establishment of the Animal Welfare Board of India, which ensures the implementation of the laws related to animal welfare in the country.
 
 
 
• **Indian Forest Act, 1927**
 
 
• This act consolidates the law relating to forests, the transit of forest-produce, and the duty leviable on timber and other forest-produce.
 
• It aims to regulate the movement of forest produce and to levy duties on timber and other forest products.
 
 
 
• **Environment Protection Act, 1986**
 
 
• This act was enacted in the aftermath of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy and aims to provide for the protection and improvement of the environment.
 
• It gives the Central Government the authority to take measures necessary to protect and improve the quality of the environment and to prevent, control, and abate environmental pollution.
